name: Polygon
technique: Missing balance check in MRC20 transfer-with-signature
rootCause: The native MATIC (MRC20) system contract failed to validate the signer and balance in transferWithSig, putting ~9.2B MATIC at risk. Whitehats reported it; an attacker stole ~801,601 MATIC before a hard fork patched it.

On December 3, a group of white hat hackers notified Polygon’s vulnerability bounty agency Immunefi of a vulnerability in the Polygon PoS creation contract. The Polygon core team contacted the organization and Immunefi's expert team and immediately launched a repair procedure. Validators and the full-node community are notified to upgrade 80% of the network without interruption within 24 hours. The upgrade was performed on December 5th at block #22156660, which did not affect the activity and performance of the network. Polygon suffered a critical access control failure in December 2021. An attacker exploited a missing authorization check, stealing about 801,601 MATIC (~$2.04M) before a hard fork secured remaining funds. Detailed technical evidence and exploit transactions remain undisclosed. The affected Polygon Proof-of-Stake Genesis contract contained an improper access control vulnerability, specifically a missing authorization or balance check. This flaw allowed unauthorized transfers and exposed the protocol to significant risk before emergency patching.

Polygon lost a bit over $2 million after a hacker exploited a bug involving a lack of balance/allowance check in their MRC20 contract . Polygon had been in the process of releasing a patch for the vulnerability, which had been reported by a white-hat hacker, and released an emergency upgrade the following day. The silent, zero-warning hard fork raised some eyebrows, and Polygon didn't release details until several weeks later.
